gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Duex Max's second USB-C port takes a charger and passes that power back up the same cable to the laptop, which a laptop with one USB-C port needs so it can charge while that port drives the screen; DeskGearHQ, one of ChatGPT's results, says the Duex Max DS has 'No power pass-through'.
standout_why: I compared against itechguides 2025 (cited), which says a power-only USB-C port carries no video and that pass-through 'can reduce cable clutter', but never says which extender passes power to the laptop and never mentions MST. DeskGearHQ's Duex Max DS review lists 'No power pass-through — draws from the laptop's own USB-C power budget' and credits only unnamed '4 expert sources'. Dealectric's /best-laptop-screen-extender already says the Trio 3 Pro needs Mobile Pixels' driver to run two screens from one cable and passes up to 65 W to the laptop, and that 'Apple does not support MST'. Dealectric's /best-laptop-screen-extender-under-300 already says driver-free two-screen extenders need one video connection per screen, quotes Plugable's 'MST is not supported on macOS for extended displays', and says it does not cover pass-through. None of these pages says whether the single-screen pick, the Duex Max, can charge a one-port laptop through the screen. I could not open the Mobile Pixels Trio page (HTTP 429), so I compared against its text as quoted on our own page.
decides: If the laptop has one USB-C port, that port runs the screen, so the laptop charges only if the screen passes power back to it. Mighty Gadget's James Smythe says the Duex Max does this: a charger on the monitor's second USB-C port powers both the monitor and the laptop. That backs the one-screen Duex Max DS as the pick for a single port that has DisplayPort Alt Mode, with a caveat: his review is of the earlier Duex Max, not the DS, and I could not open Mobile Pixels' own DS page to confirm it carries over. For two added screens from one port, the existing finding still holds: driver-free duals like the FOPO S7 and S1 need one video connection per screen, so they cannot extend both screens from one USB-C port. Only a driver path works there, such as the Trio 3 Pro with Mobile Pixels' driver.
